evidence: Browsing a category never writes to the profile — there is no setLocation or autoSyncLocation call in AllCategories or CategoryListing; the radius choice is kept in localStorage and the notification radius stays where Settings put it.

Migration 20260986 adds category_counts_nearby, which counts active listings per category inside the radius in the database; getCategoryCounts calls it and keeps the old client tally only as a fallback. It used to select every active business and provider row and count them in the browser. Forced-rollback tested on staging (before 42883, after 4 category rows).

A category page now matches every level beneath it (recursive descendantIds), so a listing filed under a sub-sub-category appears under its parent; picking a subcategory includes that branch's own children.
Businesses and providers page independently through their own cursors and render in separate sections, so loading more of one doesn't reshuffle the other.

CategoryListing passes `user.lat || undefined`, so with no location the query is simply unbounded rather than silently centred on Pune; the default coordinates are only used to render a distance label.
An empty category offers the radius control and the sibling categories rather than dead-ending, and with C3 a parent category now includes everything beneath it.
The header shows the category (and the chosen subcategory) with a back control; findCategoryNode resolves the node so the title is the real category name, not the id.
proposeCategory uses the id the insert returns; the onboarding flows record the same behaviour ('the proposed row's own id and name are used when the insert succeeds', BUSINESS_ONBOARDING #15).

Migration 20260986 adds search_businesses_nearby / search_providers_nearby: bounded by radius (ST_DWithin), ordered nearest first then by rating, with a stable id tiebreak, and discoveryService.search uses them whenever coordinates are known. Verified on staging: a shop 500 km outside the radius is excluded, one inside is found.

The same functions match the listing's name, its category, its sub-category and its catalog items' names and descriptions — verified on staging by finding Test Salon One through 'Test Haircut', a catalog item.
A trending chip reads in the viewer's language but searches the English term (translations.en[key]) — listings are written in English, so a Hindi or Marathi chip used to return nothing.
Open-now is applied as a display filter over results that are already fetched, and the screen says when everything nearby is currently closed instead of showing a bare zero-result screen.

saveSearch throws 'Sign in to save a search and get told when something new matches it' for a signed-out visitor, and the screen shows that message — it used to return silently and still toast success.
The query is mirrored into ?q= (replace, debounced) and read back on mount, so a search can be shared, bookmarked and restored by back/forward.
Shops and services page through separate cursors into separate sections, so 'Load more' on one doesn't shift the other.
Results are already grouped into labelled Shops and Services sections; tabs would add a second navigation model over the same two groups. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The input sits in a role=search form with type=search and enterKeyHint=search, and submitting blurs it, so the phone keyboard shows a search key and closes on it.
Same guest branch as GUEST_BROWSING G3: LocationPickerSheet keeps a guest's choice locally instead of calling userService.setLocation and failing with 401.
Home's nearby queries key their cache by rounded coordinates (catListingGeoKey-style geo keys), so moving city doesn't serve another city's rail from cache.
Home's realtime subscriptions are user-scoped (filter user_id=eq.<uid>) and the personal queries are skipped for guests, so a guest mount doesn't fan out personal requests.
The rails pass the viewer's own coordinates or nothing at all; the default location is used for a distance label, not to pretend the viewer is in Pune.
A failed rail shows its loading and error states (nearbyRailLoading, ErrorView with retry) instead of the section quietly disappearing.
Shops and service providers are ranked by the viewer's interests and rendered as their own rails (rankByInterests over nearbyBiz / nearbyProv), not mixed into one list.
grep '#fff' in Home.tsx: none (2026-09-16).

Recentre no longer writes the profile: the comment at MapControllers records that it used to call userService.setLocation() and refreshUser(), permanently moving the user's home point, and threw 401 for a guest. It now only moves the camera.
Pin drop keeps a guest's choice locally (the same guest branch as G3/H1) instead of throwing 401, and a long-press no longer fires a location write straight away.

The map draws the nearby set for the current viewport and radius; clustering and paging past that is a map-rendering feature, not a correctness gap, at v1 listing densities. Deferred to v1.1 under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
src/screens/MapView/mapboxFallback.ts exists for exactly this: when the tile source fails or no Mapbox token is set, the map falls back rather than leaving a blank canvas.
'Search this area' (SearchThisArea.tsx) ties the camera to the results — panning offers a re-search rather than silently leaving the sheet showing the old set.
MapSheet handles its own drag gestures with overscroll containment, so dragging the sheet doesn't fight the browser's pull-to-refresh.
grep '#fff' in src/screens/MapView: none (2026-09-16) — pins and popups use tokens from mapPalette.ts.
/place/new sits inside ProtectedLayout, so a signed-out visitor is sent to sign in before the form rather than losing a filled-in submission.
uploadService.upload compresses images before upload, so a full-resolution camera photo no longer exceeds the storage limit.
The detail screen labels the distance with the place's own city ('Distance from <city>', or 'Distance from the city' when unknown) instead of hardcoding Indore.
The submission includes the submitter's city, so places can be filtered and labelled by city; it used to be left out of the payload entirely.

A submitter sees the outcome through the notification an admin decision sends (trg_admin_audit_places / notify on status change), but there is no 'my submissions' screen with feedback and editing. That screen is a v1.1 feature, deferred under decision D17 (owner to confirm).
The form refuses to submit without a dropped pin ('Drop a pin for the location'), so coordinates are chosen deliberately rather than defaulting to wherever the submitter is standing.
discoveryService.places is bounded (limit 200) instead of downloading every active place row on each call.
grep '#fff' in src/screens/places: none (2026-09-16); the form revokes its object URLs and clears the file input after each pick.
